## ✨ Highlights

- 🔗 **Clusters**: a group of nodes the Controller keeps alike - one HAProxy configuration in versions, applied member by member; stick tables replicated between the members over mutual TLS; certificates and keys carried from member to member, never through the Controller; VRRP, BGP and the firewall from templates rendered for each member; and each member locked against changes made behind the cluster's back. A new **Clusters** tab drives them ([clusters](https://janus.sw-servers.net/docs/guide/clusters.md)).
- 🧩 **Clusters without a Controller**: `janusctl cluster` runs them from a fleet's context, on the Controller's own engine ([without a Controller](https://janus.sw-servers.net/docs/guide/clusters.md#without-a-controller)).
- ♻️ **Recycling a cluster's members**: a member replaced by a new one - a new machine like it, on a newer release or another image - and the traffic moves **once**: the newcomer joins out of service, learns the stick tables, then takes the member's place ([recycling a member](https://janus.sw-servers.net/docs/guide/clusters.md#recycling-a-member)).
- 🔁 **Replacing a node by another, its state carried**: its HAProxy configuration and history, files, certificates, Let's Encrypt, settings - exported from one node, imported into a new one, nothing through the Controller ([replacing a node](https://janus.sw-servers.net/docs/guide/replacing-a-node.md)).
- 🧷 **Stick tables survive a reload**, on every node, in a cluster or not.

## 🔄 Since the v2026.10.24 pre-release

- ♻️ **Recycling members** (below) - new ([#268](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/268)).
- What [its lab campaign](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/blob/main/docs/pre-release-tests/v2026.10.24.md) found ([#270](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/270)):
  - The member serving the traffic showed "catching up" for good - on the page, in `janusctl cluster status` and in `janus_cluster_peer_table_synced` - though its peers had everything: janusd read the wrong HAProxy counter ([#269](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/269)).
  - A node that left a cluster kept the cluster's TLS ticket keys, and the members that stayed went on using them: it now makes a ring of its own, and the others' is renewed ([#271](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/271)).

## 🔗 Clusters

What a cluster gives, and how the Controller or janusctl runs one: [clusters](https://janus.sw-servers.net/docs/guide/clusters.md); how it works: [the cluster design](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/blob/main/docs/cluster.md) ([#256](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/256), [#258](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/258), [#259](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/259), [#263](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/263), [#268](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/268), [#269](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/269), [#271](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/271)).

- **On the Controller, Clusters** (readers see them, admins change them):
  - **New cluster**: a name, the nodes, each one's member name and the address the others reach it on, and the source - its configuration becomes the cluster's version 1, its certificates and keys every member's. Checked first: the fleet, the same image, HAProxy healthy, each member reaching the others.
  - **Members**: each one's version, peers, stick tables, member certificate, drained, drifted or released; **Drain** (its virtual IPs and routes move to the others, HAProxy keeps serving), the variables its templates use, add and remove a member.
  - **Recycle** a member: by a **new machine like it** when it is one of the Controller's - same hypervisor, size, networks, extensions, at the release you give - or by a node you pick. The newcomer joins drained, gets the secrets and the version, learns the stick tables from a peer, then comes into service as the member is drained and leaves; the old machine is destroyed. A failure before the swap takes the newcomer out again. "It may run another image" lets a cluster change extensions, HAProxy branch or kernel member by member. API: `POST /api/clusters/{id}/recycle`.
  - **Configuration**: the versions, newest first; **Edit** makes a new one; **Apply** shows each file's change and what the cluster will manage, then applies it one member at a time - checked on the first member before any is touched, each member's stick tables learnt back from its peers before the next reloads (about 5 s each: members reloaded together would lose them), the first failure stops it. `haproxy.cfg`, HAProxy's files without a key, and templates for `keepalived.conf`, `bird.conf` and `firewall.nft` (`{{ .Member.Vars.priority }}`, `{{ range .Peers }}`...).
  - **Certificates**: one uploaded for every member - relayed to one member, pulled by the others. **Journal**: what was done, by whom, member by member.
  - Every 10 minutes the Controller looks at each member: a change made on a member is **reported, never overwritten** - the next apply puts it back. Member certificates are renewed, the TLS ticket key ring rotates every day.
  - The same through the API, `/api/clusters` (the guide's table), for Terraform and scripts.
- **Without a Controller** (a [fleet without a Controller](https://janus.sw-servers.net/docs/fleet-without-controller.md)), from the fleet's context:
  - `janusctl cluster create edge -source lb-1 -dir edge/ lb-1 lb-2`, then `janusctl cluster apply edge edge/` (`-dry-run`, `-manage`): the configuration is a directory - in git, say -, each apply a version.
  - `check` (exits 1 when a member wants a look - cron; renews member certificates and the ticket key ring when due), `add` (`-var`), `remove`, `replace edge lb-1 lb-4` (the same recycling, onto a node of the fleet), `delete`, `vars`, `certificate`, `tickets` (`-renew`), `journal`, `checkout`, `list`.
  - The cluster lives in the context's directory, its CA's key `0600` like the fleet's issuing key. Its members' locks are **advisory**: an administrator's certificate sending the cluster's id - what `janusctl cluster` does - gets through.
- **On the node**:
  - HAProxy's `peers janus` section is janusd's, from the node's membership: peers over mutual TLS on **TCP 10057**, with a member certificate whose key is made on the node.
  - **Locks**: a write to what the cluster manages is refused unless the Controller makes it for that cluster; `janusctl cluster release haproxy` takes it back for an emergency.
  - A member pulls the secrets from another member directly, over their own mutual TLS: uploaded certificates, files holding a key, Let's Encrypt certificates, the TLS ticket key ring.
  - **A member that leaves takes no ticket key with it**: it makes a ring of its own, and the cluster's is renewed - every key replaced - so it can neither read the tickets the cluster issues nor forge one ([TLS ticket keys](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/blob/main/docs/cluster.md#tls-ticket-keys)).
  - `janusctl cluster get | status | drain | undrain | pull | release | rotate-tickets` (`-renew`; and `csr`, `set`, `leave` for an orchestrator of your own); metrics `janus_cluster_info`, `janus_cluster_peer_up`, `janus_cluster_peer_table_synced`.

## 🔁 Replacing a node

- `janusctl -n old system state export FILE` and `janusctl -n new system state import FILE` (or one piped into the other): the node's state as files - HAProxy's configuration and its history, its files and uploaded certificates, Let's Encrypt, the TLS ticket key ring, the node's settings, its network configuration, its Controller and fleet trust ([#257](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/257)).
- The new node checks every file against the export's manifest, then restarts into it. With `-identity` it takes the old node's CA and keys - the Controller and your janusctl contexts know it as before (the old node off first); without, it is a new node with the old one's configuration.
- Its network configuration is held back unless asked for, to bring the new node up on a temporary address first and take the old one's over when ready.
- Partitions don't matter: a node installed before the LOGS partition existed moves to one that has it.
- Never through the Controller: the export carries keys.

## 🔧 HAProxy on the node

- **Stick tables survive a reload**: every node now runs HAProxy with a `peers janus` section of its own, so a table whose line ends with `peers janus` is handed from one HAProxy process to the next ([HAProxy's configuration](https://janus.sw-servers.net/docs/haproxy-config.md#the-global-section)).
- **A TLS ticket key ring** from the first boot, `/etc/haproxy/cluster/tls-ticket-keys`: a `bind` line naming it (`tls-ticket-keys /etc/haproxy/cluster/tls-ticket-keys`) resumes TLS sessions across reloads - and across a cluster's members.
- 🐛 **A certificate uploaded with SNI names is served for those names** ([#259](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/259)): HAProxy ignored the names janusd gave it, and served the certificate for the names it carries. The same certificate uploaded again no longer adds an entry to its `crt-list` each time.

## 🖥️ Controller

- The **Clusters** tab (above). A node that is a member of a cluster can't be removed from the Controller until it leaves it.
- Let's Encrypt, what v2026.10.23-2's lab found ([#253](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/253)):
  - The relay's recent tunnels show a plain-HTTP request it refuses, with its target and why.
  - An ordered certificate shows as installed as soon as it is.

## 🧪 Tests and tooling

- Real enforcing boots:
  - `qemu-cluster-test`: three nodes, peers over TLS, the stick tables after a VRRP failover and a reload, sessions resumed across members, a drain.
  - `qemu-state-migrate-test`: a node without LOGS replaced by one with it.
  - `qemu-controller-cluster-test`: a real Controller creating a cluster, locks, per-member VRRP, failover with the tables, drift, a certificate for every member, a member removed.
  - `qemu-clusterctl-test`: a janusctl fleet's cluster - advisory locks, VRRP from a directory, a dry run, drift, a certificate, a drain with the tables, a member out and back with the ticket key ring renewed, and a fourth node replacing the VRRP master with the virtual IP moving once.
  - `controller-libvirt-test`: a machine member recycled into a new machine on a real libvirt host, the old one destroyed.
  - `qemu-cluster-test` also proves that a session no longer resumes on a member that left, nor anywhere after a renewal.
- `haproxy-runtime-test` now binds a certificate for a name it doesn't carry, which proves the SNI filter.
- `qemu-hotplug-test` reads init's line even when a kernel message lands in the middle of it ([#265](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/265)).
- `hack/ui-preview.sh` makes a cluster and walks its pages, and a second preview can run beside another (`UI_PREVIEW_NAME`, `UI_PREVIEW_NET`, `UI_PREVIEW_PORT`).

## ⚠️ Upgrade notes

- **Port 10057** is HAProxy's peers port: janusd's own. A configuration with `localpeer`, its own `peers janus` section, or a `bind` on 10057 is refused - remove it before upgrading. A cluster's members reach each other on TCP 9505 and 10057: open them between members if a firewall stands between.
- **SNI names now apply**: a certificate uploaded with SNI names (the node's page, `janusctl haproxy cert-upload -sni`) is served for those names only after the upgrade, where it was served for the names it carries. Check such uploads.
- **Clusters need every member on this version**, trusting the orchestrator's fleet (the Controller's, or a `janusctl fleet`'s), on the same image. **Going back to an older version** on a member: it ignores its membership - no peers, no locks; take it out of the cluster first.
- **Replacing a node** needs both nodes on this version.
- **A member leaving a cluster** - removed, recycled, or the cluster deleted - renews the TLS ticket key rings: clients make one full TLS handshake instead of resuming their session.
- **From the v2026.10.24 pre-release**: `TLSTicketKeysRotate` now takes a request (`renew`) instead of an empty message - compatible on the wire.
